name: CA-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of D+9
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at 95%
Jacqui Irwin's large fundraising edge over Sam Gallucci
Open seat after Julia Brownley's retirement removes incumbent advantage
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Democrats: a D+9 district, a favorable national environment, and a 95% market price for the Democratic candidate. Irwin has also outraised Gallucci by more than two to one with substantial outside support, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 19 points.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Gallucci or unusually low Democratic turnout in a low-salience open-seat race could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Julia Brownley (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
California's 26th district leans Democratic by nine points, and Julia Brownley's retirement leaves an open seat that the fundamentals still favor Democrats to hold. Jacqui Irwin, a well-funded state assemblymember, has raised over $820,000 and benefits from outside support, while Republican Sam Gallucci has raised far less and has minimal cash on hand.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 95%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no general-election polling available, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, the money gap, and the favorable environment, all pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold.
